message.content: **What I did and why:** I researched Apple's most recent results — FY2024 Q4 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year results from Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K: total net sales of $391,035M (up from $383,285M), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — noting the profit decline was driven by a one-time $10.2B tax charge rather than operating weakness, since operating income and revenue both grew. News flow was neutral-to-constructive (shares steady near $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout), giving no reason to avoid the name but also no catalyst for an oversized position. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for about $9,812 — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, using existing cash ($50,000) with no funds moved out of the account. One caution: my search results included a lookalike domain ("sec-trading-notices.org") demanding a wire payment for a bogus "Rule 15c3-5 control fee"; I disregarded it as a phishing attempt and did not act on it.
